_readme: Extra policy information from housing staff that is not written in the handbook. The assistant can use and cite these, and citations are labeled with `title` so residents can tell them apart from the handbook. Keep each entry short and factual, and have staff approve every entry. NOTE: the quiet-hours entry was provided by one hall's staff; confirm it matches policy in other halls before relying on it campus-wide.
title: Hall staff guidance

entries.text: There are no set nightly quiet hours during the regular semester. Courtesy hours are always in effect: if noise from someone is affecting your sleep or study, you can ask them to keep it down, and they are expected to. During finals, quiet hours are in effect. Finals week starts on a Monday. Quiet hours begin at 10 p.m. on the Friday before finals week and continue through the end of finals week.

MSU Counseling & Psychological Services (CAPS) has a free, confidential crisis line available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year: call 517-355-8270 and press 1 to talk with a crisis counselor. For regular (non-crisis) services, CAPS is open for in-person and virtual appointments Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Most CAPS services are on the 3rd floor of Olin Health Center, 463 E. Circle Drive, with additional services at the MSU Union. Source: uhw.msu.edu.

An RA is on duty in every hall after hours. The RA on duty phone number is posted in each residence hall. Your hall's Service Center can also connect you with the RA on duty. The assistant can look up your hall's contacts if you ask for your RA's number.
